## Referee verdict

The claimed contact–diameter KKT equilibrium is valid for every local minimum, including every unrestricted global minimum. In fact, the necessary constraint qualification holds at every feasible configuration, not merely at optimizers.

However, the equilibrium equations and Delaunay edge-flip geometry do not currently yield the required unit equilateral triangle in every sufficiently large original optimizer. They leave a substantial degeneracy: contact forces may concentrate on the boundary while the entire interior remains unstressed.

I will establish the KKT statement directly, develop the exact Delaunay constraints, and exhibit explicit triangle-free stress equilibria. I will distinguish these from the additional arguments needed to solve the original problem.

The precise [Erdős Problem #99](https://www.erdosproblems.com/99?utm_source=chatgpt.com) remains listed as open. Its quantifier is over every minimum-diameter configuration of sufficiently large cardinality, not merely one optimally selected representative. Erdős Problems

A relevant recent source is Archit Das, Stress, rigidity and rhombic reductions for an Erdős minimum-diameter problem (Problem #99), September 15, 2026, DOI [10.5281/zenodo.22768362](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22768362?utm_source=chatgpt.com). Its abstract independently reports an MFCQ proof, nonnegative contact–diameter equilibrium, and rhombic reductions, while explicitly treating the original problem as open. The derivations below do not depend on accepting those claims. Zenodo

## 2. Exact Delaunay geometry of original unit contacts

### Lemma 3 — Every unit contact is a mandatory Delaunay edge

Let ∣pi−pj∣=1|p_i-p_j|=1∣pi​−pj​∣=1, and let m=(pi+pj)/2m=(p_i+p_j)/2m=(pi​+pj​)/2.

For any third site pkp_kpk​, unit separation implies

∣pk−m∣>12.|p_k-m|>\frac12.∣pk​−m∣>21​.

Indeed, if ∣pk−m∣≤1/2|p_k-m|\le1/2∣pk​−m∣≤1/2, the triangle inequality gives ∣pk−pi∣≤1|p_k-p_i|\le1∣pk​−pi​∣≤1, with equality possible only at pk=pjp_k=p_jpk​=pj​. This contradicts distinctness and unit separation.

Consequently, the closed disk with diameter pipjp_ip_jpi​pj​ contains no other original site. It is a strictly empty Gabriel disk.

In particular:

- The Voronoi cells of pi,pjp_i,p_jpi​,pj​ share a nontrivial edge.
- The contact ijijij is a Delaunay edge.
- Even with cocircular degeneracies, that unit edge occurs in every Delaunay triangulation of the original sites.

This follows directly from the empty-disk definitions of the Gabriel and Delaunay graphs. See also [Delaunay triangulations and Gabriel graphs](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary-sciences/delaunay-triangulation?utm_source=chatgpt.com). ScienceDirect Topics

Therefore, no legitimate Delaunay edge flip can remove an original unit-contact edge.

A flip exchanges the two diagonals of a convex quadrilateral in a triangulation. It does not move any of the original sites. This distinction is fundamental. DelaunayTriangulation.jl

### Lemma 4 — Contact graph restrictions

The original unit-contact graph is a simple planar straight-line graph.

For completeness, suppose two unit segments ABABAB and CDCDCD cross properly at XXX. Let

∣AX∣=x,∣BX∣=1−x,∣CX∣=y,∣DX∣=1−y.|AX|=x,\quad |BX|=1-x,\quad |CX|=y,\quad |DX|=1-y.∣AX∣=x,∣BX∣=1−x,∣CX∣=y,∣DX∣=1−y.

If x+y≤1x+y\le1x+y≤1, then

∣AC∣<x+y≤1.|AC|<x+y\le1.∣AC∣<x+y≤1.

If x+y≥1x+y\ge1x+y≥1, then

∣BD∣<(1−x)+(1−y)≤1.|BD|<(1-x)+(1-y)\le1.∣BD∣<(1−x)+(1−y)≤1.

Either contradicts unit separation.

Also, unit neighbors of a vertex must be separated by angular gaps of at least 60∘60^\circ60∘. Six unit neighbors force all six gaps to equal 60∘60^\circ60∘, producing unit equilateral triangles.

Thus a triangle-free configuration satisfies

deg⁡C(pi)≤5for every original site.(4)\boxed{\deg_C(p_i)\le5\quad\text{for every original site}.}\tag{4}degC​(pi​)≤5for every original site.​(4)

Its contact graph contains no 3-cycle, and for n≥3n\ge3n≥3 the planar girth inequality gives

∣C∣≤2n−4.(5)\boxed{|C|\le2n-4.}\tag{5}∣C∣≤2n−4.​(5)

These conclusions are exact and apply without any lattice assumption.

They are insufficient for the Erdős endpoint: a triangle-free contact graph can have nearly 2n2n2n edges, and its geometric realization can be arbitrarily close to a triangular-lattice packing.

## 3. The rhombus test: why local flips do not force a triangle

Take unit vectors

u=(1,0),v=(cos⁡θ,sin⁡θ)u=(1,0),\qquad v=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)u=(1,0),v=(cosθ,sinθ)

and the four original sites

0,u,u+v,v.0,\quad u,\quad u+v,\quad v.0,u,u+v,v.

Their four boundary distances are exactly one. The diagonal lengths are

d+=2cos⁡(θ/2),d−=2sin⁡(θ/2).d_+=2\cos(\theta/2),\qquad d_-=2\sin(\theta/2).d+​=2cos(θ/2),d−​=2sin(θ/2).

Unit separation holds exactly when

60∘≤θ≤120∘.60^\circ\le\theta\le120^\circ.60∘≤θ≤120∘.

For every

60∘<θ<120∘,60^\circ<\theta<120^\circ,60∘<θ<120∘,

neither diagonal has length one, so these four sites contain no unit equilateral triangle.

Illustrative unit-rhombus geometry. The dashed diagonals represent triangulation choices, not new physical contacts. The schematic is not to scale.

For θ≠90∘\theta\ne90^\circθ=90∘, the shorter diagonal is the Delaunay diagonal; its opposite angles sum to less than 180∘180^\circ180∘. At θ=90∘\theta=90^\circθ=90∘, both diagonals are Delaunay-compatible and can be flipped.

At the square, both diagonals have length 2\sqrt22​. Exchanging them creates no unit triangle, no new contact, and no shorter diameter.

As θ\thetaθ approaches 60∘60^\circ60∘ from above, a diagonal approaches unit length continuously, but it never equals one before the limiting angle. Hence there is no uniform positive contact-length gap that a Delaunay argument could exploit.

The missing inference is geometric motion: an edge flip alone supplies no feasible coordinate perturbation decreasing the diameter while preserving all unit-separation inequalities. The four-site quadrilateral cannot be optimized in isolation when its vertices belong to a much larger packing.

## 4. What positive tensions actually force

The equilibrium equations yield a stronger exact structural lemma than nonnegative multipliers alone.

Define the positive-contact graph

C+={ij∈C:λij>0},C^+=\{ij\in C:\lambda_{ij}>0\},C+={ij∈C:λij​>0},

and let

B={i:some ij∈H has μij>0}B=\{i:\text{some }ij\in H\text{ has }\mu_{ij}>0\}B={i:some ij∈H has μij​>0}

be the vertices carrying positive diametral loads.

### Theorem 5 — Harmonic confinement of stressed components

Let SSS be the vertex set of a connected component of C+C^+C+ containing at least one edge. Then

pi∈conv⁡{pb:b∈S∩B}(i∈S).(6)\boxed{ p_i\in\operatorname{conv}\{p_b:b\in S\cap B\} \qquad(i\in S). }\tag{6}pi​∈conv{pb​:b∈S∩B}(i∈S).​(6)

Consequently:

1. Every nontrivial positive-contact component contains at least two diametrally loaded vertices.
2. A component containing exactly two such vertices is collinear.
3. Every noncollinear positive-contact component contains at least three diametrally loaded vertices.

Proof. At every i∈S∖Bi\in S\setminus Bi∈S∖B, equilibrium gives

∑j:ij∈C+λij(pi−pj)=0.\sum_{j:ij\in C^+}\lambda_{ij}(p_i-p_j)=0.j:ij∈C+∑​λij​(pi​−pj​)=0.

Since each coefficient is positive,

pi=∑jλijpj∑jλij.(7)p_i= \frac{\sum_j\lambda_{ij}p_j} {\sum_j\lambda_{ij}}.\tag{7}pi​=∑j​λij​∑j​λij​pj​​.(7)

Thus pip_ipi​ is a weighted average of its positive-contact neighbors.

Fix any linear functional ℓ:R2→R\ell:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb Rℓ:R2→R. The scalar values ℓ(pi)\ell(p_i)ℓ(pi​) satisfy the same weighted harmonic equation outside BBB.

By the finite-graph maximum principle, the maximum and minimum over a connected positive-weight graph occur on BBB, unless the scalar function is constant. If BBB is empty, both coordinate functions are constant, contradicting the existence of a unit edge.

Therefore every ℓ(pi)\ell(p_i)ℓ(pi​) lies between its extreme values on S∩BS\cap BS∩B. The separating-hyperplane characterization of a convex hull proves (6).

If S∩BS\cap BS∩B has only one point, (6) makes all vertices coincide, again impossible. If it has exactly two points, (6) confines the whole component to their segment. □\square□

This lemma is valid for every original local minimizer and makes no assumption about contact-graph density.

### Corollary 6 — An exact restriction on unique-diameter optimizers

If a local minimum has exactly one diametral pair, ababab, then:

D is an integer,\boxed{D\text{ is an integer},}D is an integer,​

and its positive-contact graph is exactly a consecutive straight unit-contact path from pap_apa​ to pbp_bpb​.

Proof. Since ∑Cλij=D2>0\sum_C\lambda_{ij}=D^2>0∑C​λij​=D2>0, at least one positive-contact component exists. Theorem 5 implies every such component contains both aaa and bbb.

Thus there is precisely one nontrivial component, and all its vertices lie on [pa,pb][p_a,p_b][pa​,pb​].

Order these vertices along the segment. Unit separation makes consecutive gaps at least one. Since the positive-contact graph is connected and every positive edge has length exactly one, each consecutive gap must equal one. Hence the vertices form a unit-spaced path, with a,ba,ba,b at its ends, and

∣pa−pb∣=D∈Z.|p_a-p_b|=D\in\mathbb Z.∣pa​−pb​∣=D∈Z.

□\square□

This is a genuine exact necessary condition, but not a solution of Problem 99. A sufficiently large optimizer could have many diametral pairs, and a positive-contact component suspended from three or more loaded vertices can be two-dimensional without containing any unit triangle.

### Theorem 7 — First-order freezing on the stress support

Suppose uiu_iui​ is a velocity field satisfying

(pi−pj)⋅(ui−uj)≥0(ij∈C)(p_i-p_j)\cdot(u_i-u_j)\ge0 \quad(ij\in C)(pi​−pj​)⋅(ui​−uj​)≥0(ij∈C)

and

(pi−pj)⋅(ui−uj)≤0(ij∈H).(p_i-p_j)\cdot(u_i-u_j)\le0 \quad(ij\in H).(pi​−pj​)⋅(ui​−uj​)≤0(ij∈H).

Multiply the inequalities by λij\lambda_{ij}λij​ and μij\mu_{ij}μij​, respectively. Equilibrium implies

Both sums vanish. Since each summand has the indicated sign, every positive-stress edge satisfies

(pi−pj)⋅(ui−uj)=0whenever λij>0 or μij>0.(8)\boxed{ (p_i-p_j)\cdot(u_i-u_j)=0 \quad\text{whenever }\lambda_{ij}>0 \text{ or }\mu_{ij}>0. }\tag{8}(pi​−pj​)⋅(ui​−uj​)=0whenever λij​>0 or μij​>0.​(8)

Thus all positive-stress active edges are infinitesimally frozen for any first-order feasible, non-diameter-increasing motion.

But this says nothing about zero-stress unit contacts, and it does not exclude second-order improvements along a direction where every first derivative vanishes.

That is the central weakness of using first-order equilibrium alone.

## 5. An infinite adversarial family: exact KKT, no triangles, not even local minima

Here is a concrete test of any proposed inference from equilibrium to optimality or triangles.

For each odd integer m≥3m\ge3m≥3, take the original sites

Pm={(i,j):0≤i,j≤m−1,i,j∈Z}.P_m=\{(i,j):0\le i,j\le m-1,\ i,j\in\mathbb Z\}.Pm​={(i,j):0≤i,j≤m−1,i,j∈Z}.

There are n=m2n=m^2n=m2 sites, their minimum separation is one, and their diameter is

Dm=2(m−1).D_m=\sqrt2(m-1).Dm​=2​(m−1).

The only unit contacts are the horizontal and vertical nearest-neighbor edges, so there are no unit equilateral triangles.

### Exact KKT certificate for every mmm

There are exactly two diametral pairs, joining opposite corners. Assign multiplier 1/21/21/2 to each.

Assign contact multiplier

w=m−12w=\frac{m-1}{2}w=2m−1​

to every unit edge along the outer square boundary, and zero to every other contact.

These weights satisfy every KKT equation:

- At a noncorner boundary vertex, the two equal tangential contact forces cancel.
- At an interior vertex, all positive stresses vanish.
- At each corner, the two side forces sum to exactly half the displacement vector toward the opposite corner, with the correct orientation.

The normalization is exact:

∑Hμ=1,∑Cλ=4(m−1)w=2(m−1)2=Dm2.\sum_H\mu=1,\qquad \sum_C\lambda=4(m-1)w =2(m-1)^2=D_m^2.H∑​μ=1,C∑​λ=4(m−1)w=2(m−1)2=Dm2​.

Hence the configuration satisfies precisely the nonnegative equilibrium derived for local optimizers.

The construction works for arbitrarily large n=m2n=m^2n=m2, with an interior unstressed sector of cardinality (m−2)2(m-2)^2(m−2)2.

## 6. Conditional rhombic-face counting

There is a valid structural reduction from a very dense triangle-free contact graph to rhombuses.

Assume the unit-contact graph is connected and its bounded faces have simple cycle boundaries. Let eee be its number of edges, and let bbb be the length of its outer-face boundary walk.

Euler's formula gives finner=e−n+1f_{\mathrm{inner}}=e-n+1finner​=e−n+1, and the sum of the bounded face lengths is 2e−b2e-b2e−b. Therefore

∑Fbounded(∣∂F∣−4)=4n−4−2e−b.(11)\boxed{ \sum_{F\ {\rm bounded}}(|\partial F|-4) =4n-4-2e-b. }\tag{11}Fbounded∑​(∣∂F∣−4)=4n−4−2e−b.​(11)

Every face length is at least four in a triangle-free contact graph.

Thus, if one additionally proves

e=2n−O(n),b=O(n),e=2n-O(\sqrt n),\qquad b=O(\sqrt n),e=2n−O(n​),b=O(n​),

then the total excess face length is O(n)O(\sqrt n)O(n​), implying that all but O(n)O(\sqrt n)O(n​) bounded faces are quadrilaterals.

A simple quadrilateral with four unit sides is a rhombus. Each such face must have its angle strictly between 60∘60^\circ60∘ and 120∘120^\circ120∘ to avoid a unit triangle.

This is consistent with the rhombic reductions described in Das's September 2026 preprint. Zenodo

But the two quantitative hypotheses are essential. Neither follows from arbitrary nonnegative KKT multipliers. In particular, the square-grid example has 2n−O(n)2n-O(\sqrt n)2n−O(n​) contacts and entirely quadrilateral bounded faces, yet contains no unit triangle.

A rhombic-face reduction is therefore not an exact endpoint unless coupled to additional global diameter constraints or a rigorous boundary-pinning impossibility theorem.

## 7. Why common stress and rigidity upgrades fail

### The signed-stress quadratic form cannot be globally positive semidefinite

One tempting method is to turn the KKT equilibrium into a universal diameter certificate.

Define

Q(u)=∑Hμij∣ui−uj∣2−∑Cλij∣ui−uj∣2.Q(u)= \sum_H\mu_{ij}|u_i-u_j|^2 -\sum_C\lambda_{ij}|u_i-u_j|^2.Q(u)=H∑​μij​∣ui​−uj​∣2−C∑​λij​∣ui​−uj​∣2.

If Q(u)≥0Q(u)\ge0Q(u)≥0 for every configuration of vectors uiu_iui​, the inequalities for arbitrary unit-separated sites could furnish a global lower-diameter certificate.

But for KKT weights this is impossible whenever D>1D>1D>1.

The signed graph Laplacian representing QQQ has trace

tr⁡L=2(∑Hμij−∑Cλij)=2(1−D2)<0.\operatorname{tr}L =2\left(\sum_H\mu_{ij}-\sum_C\lambda_{ij}\right) =\boxed{2(1-D^2)<0}.trL=2(H∑​μij​−C∑​λij​)=2(1−D2)<0​.

A positive-semidefinite matrix cannot have negative trace.

Thus no KKT equilibrium for D>1D>1D>1 can yield this straightforward global positive-semidefinite stress certificate.

### Exact limitation

The theorem controls deformation of a known, connected, near-equilateral triangular-lattice mesh. Its proof does not require all the edges to be exact unit contacts.

It does not establish any of the following for an arbitrary global optimizer:

- The existence of a spanning triangular-lattice reference mesh.
- Uniform connectivity and shape regularity of its near-equilateral region.
- A uniform Korn constant through holes, cracks, interfaces, or narrow necks.
- A prescribed boundary displacement or a diameter-decreasing variation.

In particular, it would be invalid to apply (17) to the complete original contact graph merely because that graph is planar.

The quantitative estimate is valid; the step converting it into a strict same-nnn diameter improvement remains unproved.

The main unresolved implication can now be stated more sharply.

For a sufficiently large purported triangle-free global optimizer, the available tools provide an exact boundary–area–seam accounting identity, nonnegative local defects on controlled faces, and an exact stress equilibrium. To obtain a contradiction, one still needs to prove that these conditions force one of two outcomes: either an original equilateral contact is present, or there exists a finite, unit-separated same-cardinality perturbation with smaller diameter.

The two principal unresolved obstacles are distinct.

First, there is the geometric coercivity gap. Seam incidence is extensive, but seam excess can approach zero. The area estimate gives upper bounds on total strain, not a positive lower bound independent of seam lengths. Moreover, exceptional Delaunay faces can carry negative defects, and Korn constants can deteriorate on domains with poorly controlled interfaces.

Second, there is the diameter transversality gap. Even if a connected bulk patch is close to a triangular lattice, neither the density identity nor geometric rigidity specifies a deformation that contracts every active diameter pair while respecting the original contact inequalities. KKT equilibrium expressly rules out the simplest first-order strategy.

A viable next theorem would need to link the stress weights on the original contacts to the global interface geometry and active diameter pairs, with enough second-order information to establish a genuine nonlinear diameter improvement. The current identities do not supply that link.

The strongest defensible result is a conditional reduction.

Assume, for all sufficiently large nnn, one could establish both of the following:

- No isolated unrestricted global optimizer is triangle-free.
- No positive-dimensional component of the unrestricted global optimizer space contains any triangle-free point.

Then every unrestricted global optimizer for those nnn necessarily contains a unit equilateral triangle.

The argument is rigorous: any putative triangle-free optimizer must fall into one of the two cases, and each has been excluded.

For the second exclusion, local rigidity of isolated components says nothing about positive-dimensional components. Even if every such component contains some triangle-bearing configurations, triangle-free points could occupy an open region of that same component.

The persistent-triangle lemma from Section 3 offers one possible attack: demonstrate that every positive-dimensional analytic optimizer stratum has a permanently unit-equilateral triple. But no such theorem has been proved for arbitrary large-nnn global optima.

There is an exact necessary-and-sufficient Farkas criterion for lifting any prescribed first-order deformation of the original packing to a feasible second-order jet. At an unrestricted global diameter minimizer, it yields a rigorous spectral instability test and a stronger stress-support reduction.

The criterion detects an explicit diameter-decreasing deformation of every square grid of side length at least three. It also passes the globally optimal, triangle-free eight-point regular-heptagon configuration.

It does not establish that every sufficiently large global minimizer contains an exact unit equilateral triangle. The missing step is a universal argument producing a destabilizing critical direction in every sufficiently large triangle-free global minimizer.

The principal mathematical results below are my own deductions from finite-dimensional optimization and Farkas duality, except where published or earlier preprint results are expressly identified.

### 4.2 Actual lifting versus formal lifting

Theorem 1 concerns second-order jets.

If all the relevant inequalities in (4.2)–(4.3) are strict, the quadratic path itself is feasible for sufficiently small positive sss. Every inactive constraint remains feasible by continuity.

If some second-order inequalities hold with equality, cubic or higher-order terms can decide feasibility. Accordingly, a non-strict formal jet is not automatically an actual C2C^2C2 curve of unit-separated packings.

This distinction is indispensable: second-order Farkas feasibility is necessary and sufficient at the level of the second-order inequalities, not at the level of arbitrary exact nonlinear continuation.

The twelve-cap construction solves three collision classes for its own lattice packing: new–new within a frame, new–new across frames, and new–retained-lattice.
